title: Game vision
author: Alternative-Fun-2880
selftext: How do you give eyes to your models ? I’m not using Astra yet , I have Claude . But the problem is the same . I see llm able to do magic’s , the create game from scratch, but is an llm able to watch a game ? He can surely reed an image and analyse it . But how do you make a model really watch a game session ?

comments.author: StrongCucumber
comments.body:
Lately I've been observing the code of an old game to help me with some of the mechanics I want in my own one. I've decompiled the original with Ghidra and I'm letting Claude studying it, in addition it just asks me to launch the proper game and do stuff on it, when I do Claude creates is own instruments, registers what I'm doing on the running exe and compares it with the code and his own dry data/previsions.

I've no idea if it's simpler than this, I'd be curios to know.

comments.author: Gambo7592
comments.body: Im not sure how it works but when I give claude like a reference Pic or even video it's able to describe to me what it "saw" no clue how that works

comments.author: amoeb4
comments.body: You could try with video (never tried it myself tbh), but with Astra I have noticed that to ensure sure mechanics are implemented correctly, it creates tests that capture screenshots of implemented mechanic, so then it can analyse the screenshots and based on them decide if everything is ok or not

comments.author: KnownPride
comments.body:
What you mean watch game session? 
You should do it yourself as only you can judge does the ai result is based on your vision or not. 

It's like Judging employees work result.

comments.author: Alternative-Fun-2880
comments.body: The request is to improve the context of the llm. A static game can be easily evaluated with a screen but what if there is a bug during a 60 frame animation ? Currently the only stuff I could think of is sending 60 frame of the anim but of course this is not scalable. But I’m not sure if I send a 5 min video of the gameplay ir will be able to identify the issue without pointing at a specify time frame
